name: Molecular SO2
seoTitle: Molecular SO2 Calculator: Free, With Steps
seoDesc: Molecular SO2: work out molecular SO₂ from the free SO₂ and the wine pH. A free food calculator with the formula, units and a worked example.
summary: Give the Molecular SO2 calculator the free SO₂, the wine pH and the desired molecular SO₂ and it returns molecular SO₂. Think of it as a shortcut for portioning, timing or nutrition. The formula is printed further down, so you can check the answer by hand if you want to.

sections.title: How does the Molecular SO2 calculator work?
sections.html:
The Molecular SO2 calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports molecular SO₂ in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you type in the free SO₂, the wine pH and the desired molecular SO₂.

Press Calculate once and the page holds the relationship, tracking which boxes you filled and working out everything else; from that point on it follows every edit you make.

sections.title: The formula behind the Molecular SO2 calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Molecular SO₂=(100 × free SO₂ ÷ ((10 ^ wine pH + 19 ÷ 100) + 100))
Required free SO₂=((1 ÷ 100) × desired molecular SO₂ × ((10 ^ wine pH + 19 ÷ 100) + 100))

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

Before doubting the arithmetic, check the inputs: a unit chip on the wrong setting, a drop-down left at its default, or a percentage typed as a whole number rather than a decimal will each shift the answer by a clean power of ten.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Molecular SO2 calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Checking portions before you shop
  • Scaling a recipe up or down
  • Working out timing so everything finishes together
  • Any time the same 3 figures keep coming back — the free SO₂, the wine pH and the desired molecular SO₂ — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html: • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

sections.title: What are the limits worth knowing?
sections.html:
Every tool draws a boundary somewhere. For the Molecular SO2 calculator, these are the ones that matter:

  • The calculator reports what the relationship implies; it does not judge whether the inputs themselves are sensible, so a figure that is out by a factor of ten will produce an answer that is out by the same factor.

sections.title: How do you check the answer yourself?
sections.html:
• Change one input at a time — free SO₂ for instance — and watch which results move. A result that stays put does not depend on it.
  • Try a round value you can work out in your head. If the answer matches your mental arithmetic, the inputs are on the scale you assumed.
  • Re-enter the same figure and confirm the result is stable; a number that moves when you press Calculate again is a sign that a field is still empty.

faq.q: What does the Molecular SO2 calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns molecular SO₂, derived from the free SO₂, the wine pH and the desired molecular SO₂. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Molecular SO2 calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the free SO₂, the wine pH and the desired molecular SO₂, which is 3 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Is the Molecular SO2 calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — press Calculate and every result updates together.

faq.q: Why is the answer different from the one in my protocol?
faq.a: Nearly always a unit or a rounding difference. The calculator works in the units printed next to each box, keeps full precision internally and only rounds for display, so recomputing from the rounded numbers on screen can differ in the last digit.

faq.q: Can I use the numbers straight from a datasheet?
faq.a: Yes. Every box states its unit and nothing is converted behind your back, so a figure copied from a datasheet, a kit insert or a protocol goes in as printed.
